title: Tech Note: New Variable Declaration
author: Bryan Yen, Technical Services Engineer, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Autocomplete / type-ahead in the code editor

historical_commentary.text: The 'var' typed-declaration syntax introduced around v18R4 became 4D's standard, recommended way to declare variables and has only become more entrenched since, fully superseding the older C_TEXT/C_OBJECT-style 'Compiler theme' directives for new code; this note's guidance is still accurate and describes what remains current best practice.
related_updates: 'var' with typed class references (4D.ClassName / cs.ClassName) is now the standard, encouraged variable declaration style in current 4D versions
Old C_TEXT/C_OBJECT/C_LONGINT-style Compiler theme declarations are still supported for compatibility but are considered legacy style for new development
Arrays and inter-process variables mentioned as unsupported by 'var' at the time remain declared via the older Array/Compiler theme commands, as arrays are a distinct 4D language concept
